problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Given One Basis
examples.problem:
Consider the basis $\mathcal{B}=\{\mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3\}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $\mathcal{C}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/7c123e6f7d842a8e86e4c99826d25df070982514960752a25481a9f3f046cc1b.png)

Find the matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ of the map $\mathbf{T}:V \to \mathbb{R}^2$ relative to these bases if 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/9a469219c661453d7891935b2ef0a32bff972bcf903d641ca7e31b7bec26369a.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1),$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2),$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_i)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/9d774b5bd79f14bc31e88a649fcb2a682d94ae3dd8acde5e25f52369c136e11e.png)

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 1 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 & 3 & -7 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 & 3 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -8 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 11 & -29 & 25 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -8 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{C} \mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/778f179c4681bcdcc5a64bcd128d946a272fa869289d2c2e542df75ad05850b6.png)

feedback.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$ Therefore,

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 0 \\ -5 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$
